description: We're a team of three Bachelor's students from different academic backgrounds, bringing together diverse perspectives, skills and ideas. We're excited to work on the Astronaut Health Monitoring challenge and develop an innovative, user-friendly solution to support astronaut health during space missions. We're looking for motivated teammates interested in programming, data analysis, engineering, healthcare, biology or UI/UX design. Let's build something meaningful for the future space exploration
summary:
SpaceMax is a smart astronaut health monitoring and authentication platform designed to support astronaut safety during space missions. We developed a web-based system that combines secure face-based authentication with a centralized health monitoring dashboard. Using OpenCV and SFace facial recognition, the system generates face embeddings and communicates with a backend API to verify registered users. Once authenticated, astronauts can access their personalized dashboard, where sensor data can be collected, processed, and interpreted to monitor health-related parameters.
The project addresses the challenge by exploring how digital technologies, biometric authentication, and sensor-based monitoring can contribute to astronaut health and mission safety. By bringing authentication and health information together in one platform, SpaceMax aims to make health monitoring more accessible, organized, and efficient. It also features cognitive mini-games to encourage mental activity and help astronauts stay engaged during long-duration space missions.
This is crucial because astronauts operate in demanding environments where continuous awareness of health conditions is essential. SpaceMax demonstrates how accessible software technologies and data-driven solutions can contribute to safer and more informed human space exploration.
details:
SpaceMax is a health monitoring system that collects, organizes, and visualizes astronaut health data. It brings

multiple health indicators together in one system, allowing users to examine measurements and track changes

over time. In addition of SQLite and local JSON files, SpaceMax utilizes a robust and relational PostgreSQL

database. Rather than automatically generating a new data set for each user, the system allows health data to be

imported via CSV files. Thanks to this flexible structure, testers and administrators can upload pre-prepared CSV

data sets containing specific custom scenarios and edge conditions (such as abnormal vitals or cardiovascular

stress), enabling them to test all desired use cases in a controlled and reproducible manner. The collected data

are presented through a Tkinter-based interface, using health indicators, graphs, and measurement tables to

make changes in astronauts' health easier to track and understand.
